Task 3 In Holocene’s integrated DAC process, the crystallization step allows transferring the CO from the liquid 2 phase to a solid phase that can be separated out. Once separated, the liquid can be recycled back to the absorption unit. The guanidine salt solid collected can then be processed for recovery of the CO gas and 2 further recycling of the regenerated guanidine free base solid in the crystallization. As a consequence, the performance of the solid-liquid separation, further referred to as “separation”, directly impacts the performance of the whole process. The performance of the separation can be assessed in different ways, including by measuring the residual moisture content in the solid phase. Lower residual moisture contents allow for recovering and recycling more of the liquid phase, while reducing the need for post-processing of the wet solid. Lower residual moisture contents result from a combination of factors of the separation technology itself, but also of the 6 suspensions properties, defined by the crystallization operation taking place upstream. Typically, the solids content (amount of solid per volume of liquid), and the particle shapes and sizes are the suspension properties that have the largest impact on the separation. In this project, a target residual moisture content has been defined as a success criterion for the separation. In order to reach this target, research activities were divided into 2 subtasks: • Subtask 3.1. Validating Crystallization Process Parameters • Subtask 3.2 Conceptual Design of Crystallization Process Task 3.1 In order to investigate crystallization process parameters at the “smallest meaningful scale”, a testbench system was designed, built & commissioned; experimental campaigns with that testbench allowed for the following crystallization properties to be recorded: • Thermodynamics data of the chemical system over a range of pH and temperatures relevant to the process design • Kinetics data of the chemical system collected on suspension generated in batch and continuous crystallization modes • Impact of mixing geometry on suspension homogeneity • PSSD of suspensions generated in batch crystallization mode with seeding and BIG FB solid feed rate control • Identifying the kinetic parameter of the crystal studied was idenitfied, and confirmed the chemical system yields smaller particles at shorter residence times in continuous crystallization • PSSD of suspensions generated in continuous crystallization mode • Identification of post-treatment of PSSD of continuous crystallization to reduce their aspect ratio The activities carried in this subtask lead to significant learnings on the chemical system and its behavior during crystallization and separation. It was identified that the PSD of the carbonate salt crystals come with the drawback of high aspect ratio crystals. It was found that the moisture content in the solids after separation is strongly dependent on the aspect ratio of the crystal. 7 This morphology and its impact on filtration performance was mitigated by investigating a pathway to reduce the aspect ratio by post treating the suspension from the continuous crystallization.
